Patient segment / dependency: Steroid and MMF/CNI-dependent or biologic-inadequate responders; high IFN/B-cell signatures
Target candidates: CD40L, IFNAR1, BAFF-R, FcRn, APRIL, CD19-FcGR2B
Evidence / rationale: Autoantibody, immune-complex and T-B costimulation biology; approved belimumab/anifrolumab leave incomplete renal and steroid-sparing responses; CD40L and FcRn phase 2/3 activity ongoing.
Concerns: Very heterogeneous; endpoint noise; infection/thrombosis risk; crowded B-cell/IFN space.

Patient segment / dependency: Systemic active disease, ESSDAI-high, B-cell/IgG/FcRn-high, fatigue-pain subgroup separated
Evidence / rationale: Nipocalimab, ianalumab and dazodalibep trials validate antibody tractability; no broadly approved disease-modifying therapy in many regions; biomarker-rich B-cell disease.
Concerns: Sicca/fatigue endpoints hard; irreversible gland damage; placebo response; competition increasing.

Patient segment / dependency: Early diffuse cutaneous, inflammatory/CCL24-high, ILD-risk, steroid-avoidance population
Evidence / rationale: Fibrosis/inflammation and autoantibody overlap; nintedanib slows ILD but does not reverse disease; CCL24 and B-cell agents in trials.
Concerns: Many anti-fibrotic failures; slow endpoints; tissue penetration; safety around repair/wound healing.

Evidence / rationale: Steroids work but relapses and toxicity common; inebilizumab approval and obexelimab phase 3 validate B-cell/plasmablast axis.
Concerns: CD19 space now less open; long-term hypogammaglobulinemia; organ fibrosis may be irreversible.

Patient segment / dependency: Refractory skin/muscle/ILD despite steroids, IVIG, JAKi or immunosuppressants
Evidence / rationale: Type I IFN and autoantibodies prominent; FcRn could lower pathogenic IgG without broad cytotoxicity; complement implicated in myositis tissue injury.
Concerns: Rare, heterogeneous; IVIG/JAK competition; muscle endpoints slow; infection risk.

Evidence / rationale: Complement C5aR biology clinically validated by avacopan; B-cell depletion standard but relapses persist; antibody options could target autoantibody or complement axis.
Concerns: C5aR already served by small molecule; CD20 crowded; infection/hypogammaglobulinemia.

Patient segment / dependency: Pemphigus vulgaris or bullous pemphigoid with steroid dependence or relapse
Target candidates: FcRn, CD19, CD20, CD38, IL4R, C5
Evidence / rationale: Pathogenic IgG is causal; rituximab and FcRn inhibitors support antibody-accessible biology; biomarkers include Dsg1/3 or BP180/230 titers.
Concerns: Market fragmented; FcRn increasingly crowded; infection in elderly BP; relapse after IgG lowering.

Evidence / rationale: Current AIH still relies on steroids/thiopurines; PSC lacks approved disease-modifying therapy; gut-liver trafficking and fibrosis targets are extracellular.
Concerns: AIH biology less validated for antibodies; PSC endpoints long; hepatobiliary safety; biomarkers immature.

Disease: Celiac disease / refractory or nonresponsive disease
Patient segment / dependency: Gluten-free diet nonresponse; refractory celiac disease; steroid/budesonide dependence
Target candidates: IL15, IL7R, TL1A, OX40L, TGM2 immune complexes
Evidence / rationale: IL-15 biology strong in refractory celiac; amlitelimab is in phase 2 nonresponsive celiac, validating costimulation modulation.
Concerns: Oral antigen exposure confounds endpoints; lymphoma risk in RCD-II; tissue access; small population.

Patient segment / dependency: Moderate-severe patients failing TNF/IL-17/IL-23; steroid/antibiotic/surgery dependent
Evidence / rationale: Antibody successes and failures reveal unmet need; abscess/tunnel biology has extracellular cytokine and neutrophil chemokine nodes.
Concerns: Not classic autoimmune; crowded dermatology; several IL-1/IL-36/chemokine failures; infection/wound healing.
